item.witchery.witches_primer.patchouli_m: Patchouli is required to open this book.
witchery.book.title: The Witches' Primer
witchery.book.landing: You have found - or, more likely, been given - this volume. It is not a complete record of the craft. No single book could be. But it is a beginning, and beginnings matter.$(br2)Study the rowan first. Raise an altar. Then, when you are ready, the rest will follow. Do not rush. The craft does not reward impatience, and it punishes foolishness with unusual creativity.
witchery.book.cat.getting_started.desc: All things start somewhere. Yours starts with a tree you probably walked past without noticing.
witchery.book.cat.brewing.desc: Concoctions for good or for ill - the kettle does not judge. That is your responsibility.
witchery.book.cat.circle_magic.desc: Draw the circle. Name the working. The world bends if you ask it correctly.
witchery.book.cat.poppet_magic.desc: Mystical effigies with a direct effect on whoever they are bound to. Choose your intentions carefully.
witchery.book.cat.transformations.desc: What you are is not fixed. What you become is another matter entirely.
witchery.book.cat.spirit_world.desc: The veil is thin. Step through it carefully, and learn to find your way back.
witchery.book.cat.conjuration.desc: Fire, smoke, and things that answer when called. Mind what you ask for.
witchery.book.cat.creatures.desc: Not all denizens of a witch's world are human. Most are more interesting for it.
witchery.book.entry.first_steps.page1: The craft has no grand ceremony of initiation. You begin when you begin. But there are practical requirements, and the first is the rowan tree.$(br2)The rowan, or mountain-ash, has an affinity with magic that few trees can match. It is rare in the wild - rarer than it should be, in this world - but you can coax a sapling into being with Mutandis. Once you have it, protect it.
witchery.book.entry.first_steps.page2: If the rowan is your foundation, the Altar is your hearth. It gathers magical energy from the natural world around it - rowan wood, candelabras, chalices, skulls, and other things a witch tends to accumulate.$(br2)Right-click your altar to see how much power it holds. Surround it with meaningful objects and it will grow stronger. The craft rewards those who tend their spaces.
witchery.book.entry.altar.page1: If the power of this craft has a lifeblood, the altar is the heart that circulates it. It draws energy from natural and decorative objects within a generous radius and holds it ready for the kettle, the rites, and whatever else you see fit to demand of it.$(br2)Different blocks contribute different amounts. Rowan wood, candelabras, Redstone Soup-filled chalices, placed pentagrams and athames - all feed the altar. Keep it furnished. A sparse altar is a weak altar.
witchery.book.entry.altar.recipe: Craft the altar. Then decide where it will live, because it is difficult to move and the objects around it matter.
witchery.book.entry.rowan_tree.page1: The rowan is unremarkable to look at - a slender tree with silver bark, prone to growing in unlikely places. But it carries something the other trees do not: a sympathy with the unseen world that makes it indispensable to a practising witch.$(br2)Grow one from a sapling mutated with Mutandis, or find one growing wild. Its logs feed your altar; its planks build your tools; its berries have their own quiet uses.
witchery.book.entry.rowan_tree.berries: The berries fall from the leaves in small clusters. They are not much to look at, and they taste dreadful. But they are a component in several important brews, and burning them in a brazier produces a mild healing aura. Do not discard them.
witchery.book.entry.kettle.page1: A kettle is a simple thing: a vessel, a fire, and whatever you choose to put inside it. That last part is where things get interesting.$(br2)Right-click to add your reagents one by one, then light a fire beneath the kettle. It draws power from the nearest altar to complete the working. The ingredients determine what emerges. Keep records of what you try. The craft does not always announce itself.
witchery.book.entry.kettle.recipe: Iron and a modicum of patience. That is all a kettle needs to be born.
witchery.book.entry.drop_of_luck.page1: Drop of Luck is one of those ingredients that sounds fanciful until a rite or brew refuses to work without it. In the older craft it belonged to the Witch's Cauldron, not the kettle: a harsher little working that curdles good hedge powders into something stranger.$(br2)That distinction matters, because this drop sits at the edge between ordinary mutation and the more capricious parts of Witchery.
witchery.book.entry.drop_of_luck.page2: Heat and fill a Witch's Cauldron, keep an altar nearby, drop in a $(item)Mandrake Root$(), $(item)Nether Wart$(), $(item)Tear of the Goddess$(), and $(item)Refined Evil$(), then use $(item)Mutandis Extremis$() on the cauldron itself.$(br2)The powder is spent, the altar pays the price, and a single Drop of Luck condenses from the bowl. Rewoven now follows that source-backed route again instead of the old kettle placeholder.
witchery.book.entry.witches_oven.page1: Not everything useful comes from a kettle. Some ingredients must be rendered down first - reduced, transformed, made into something the craft can actually use.$(br2)The Witches' Oven smolders logs into witches' ash, coaxes nether wart into Exhale of the Horned One, and works its patience on quartz until quicklime emerges. It will not accept ingredients that are not its concern. Do not attempt to argue with it.
witchery.book.entry.witches_oven.recipe: Iron and netherbrick, shaped with intent. The oven requires only a fire beneath and materials worth its attention.
witchery.book.entry.distillery.page1: Some essences cannot be coaxed directly from raw materials. They must be drawn out through heat and pressure - concentrated, refined, stripped of everything incidental until only the potent core remains.$(br2)The Distillery takes two inputs and fuel. It needs no altar. It is patient in a way that most tools are not. Feed it condensed fear, refined evil, the leavings of dark workings - it will reward you with something more useful.
witchery.book.entry.distillery.recipe: Iron, glass, and a brewing stand. The distillery is not complicated; what you put inside it, often is.
witchery.book.entry.chalk.page1: Before you can perform a rite, you must prepare the ground for it. The circle is not mere tradition - it is the structure that makes the working possible, a closed space in which intention and power can accumulate until they are ready to be released.$(br2)Right-click with chalk on flat stone or earth to draw a glyph. Continue around the perimeter until the ring is complete. Then place your ingredient at the center and activate with an empty hand.
witchery.book.entry.chalk.upgrades: When basic ritual chalk is no longer enough, return to the older way. Fill a heated Witch's Cauldron, drop the support ingredients into the bowl, keep an altar nearby, and use the base chalk on the cauldron itself.$(br2)$(li)Golden - Mandrake Root + Gold Nugget$(li)Infernal - Nether Wart + Blaze Powder$(li)Otherwhere - Nether Wart + Tear of the Goddess + Ender Pearl$(br2)Each working consumes altar power and transforms the offered ritual chalk into the stronger family.
witchery.book.entry.chalk.variants: Ritual chalk is the beginning. Golden chalk opens more demanding rites. Otherwhere chalk draws across the boundary of worlds. Infernal chalk speaks to things best not named lightly. Use each according to what you actually need, not what is most impressive.
witchery.book.entry.drawing_circles.page: The circle must be complete. A gap, even a small one, undoes the whole working - power spills, reagents are wasted, and the rite fails with the special indignity reserved for careless practitioners.$(br2)Right-click with chalk to place each glyph in sequence around the perimeter. When the ring closes, you will feel it. Place the activating ingredient at the center, then use an empty hand to trigger the rite.
witchery.book.entry.drawing_circles.size: $(li)$(bold)Small (3x3)$(/) - Infusions, familiar binding, personal rites and small transpositions$(li)$(bold)Medium (5x5)$(/) - Summoning, fertility, most working-scale buff rites$(li)$(bold)Large (7x7)$(/) - World-altering rites, curses, dimensional workings$(br2)The Circle Talisman stores a circle pattern and redeploys it instantly. A genuine convenience when your knees object to drawing the same ring twice.
witchery.book.entry.rites.page1: A rite is the intentional manipulation of the world through circle, ingredient, and power. The circle provides the structure; the ingredient names the working; the altar provides the fuel. Some rites also require creatures to be present nearby - not for ceremony, but because their presence is part of the mechanism.$(br2)Experimentation is encouraged. The craft does not document all of its own workings.
witchery.book.entry.rites.examples.title: A Selection
witchery.book.entry.rites.examples: $(li)$(bold)Infusion$(/) (small, infusion brew) - grants a lasting magical nature$(li)$(bold)Familiar Binding$(/) (small, Attuned Stone) - binds a tamed animal as companion$(li)$(bold)Rite of the Forest$(/) (large, any sapling) - grows a grove of magical woodland$(li)$(bold)Waystone Binding$(/) (small+medium, waystone items) - establishes teleportation anchors$(li)$(bold)Rite of Transposition$(/) (medium+large, bound waystone) - moves you or another
witchery.book.entry.taglock_kit.page1: A taglock is a thread of sympathy connecting a practitioner to their subject. Without it, poppets are merely decorative, curses fall without direction, and certain rites cannot find their target.$(br2)Right-click a living creature directly, or steal a player's sample by crouching up behind them if you can manage it. Clumsy attempts may fail and alert the target. Blood Roses, Leech Chests, and even a freshly slept-in bed can hold the same sort of sample for later theft. Guard your own sleep accordingly.
witchery.book.entry.taglock_kit.recipe: A glass bottle and a pin. Simple enough, and deliberately so - the difficulty is in what you do with it afterward.
witchery.book.entry.poppets.page1: An effigy shaped to resemble a person, bound to them through a taglock, carries a thread of the same sympathy that connects all things. What happens to the effigy has a tendency to happen to its subject. This is the basis of poppet magic, and it works in both directions.$(br2)Bind a poppet by right-clicking it with a filled taglock. Then place it on a Poppet Shelf, or carry a protection poppet in your own inventory.
witchery.book.entry.poppets.recipe: The Voodoo Poppet is the foundation of this practice. From it, other forms follow.
witchery.book.entry.poppets.protection: Protection poppets are consumed when triggered - they give themselves to prevent something worse happening to you. Death Protection, Earth, Water, Fire, Hunger - each covers a different category of misfortune. Voodoo Protection specifically counters hostile poppet workings.$(br2)Keep spares. The shelf holds nine.
witchery.book.entry.poppet_shelf.page1: A poppet kept in a pocket is useful. A poppet on a shelf that automatically activates when needed is more useful still.$(br2)The Poppet Shelf holds up to nine poppets. When you take damage or are killed, it scans nearby shelves for poppets bound to you and triggers the appropriate protection. You need not be watching. That is the point.
witchery.book.entry.poppet_shelf.recipe: Build it, fill it, and stop thinking about it. It will think for itself when the time comes.
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.page1: There are those who choose this path, and those who have it chosen for them. Either way, the nature of vampirism is not subtle: you are sustained by blood, strengthened by it, and diminished without it. Your blood level determines your power.$(br2)Drain blood from living creatures by right-clicking them. A vampire at full blood is formidable. A vampire running dry is less so.
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.abilities: $(li)Speed, strength, and reach - all scale with blood level$(li)Night vision, always$(li)A bite that takes blood from the living$(li)Resistance to most sources of damage$(li)The ability to sleep through daylight in a coffin, which is its own kind of grace
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.weaknesses: $(li)Sunlight burns - direct daylight is a persistent danger$(li)Silver wounds heal slowly and hurt more$(li)Witch Hunters consider you a professional priority$(li)Blood drains constantly. Feed regularly or suffer accordingly$(li)There is no going back, not easily
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.clothing: Woven Cruor is back as the base cloth for the vampire wardrobe. As a vampire with at least 125 blood, use a Bone Needle on placed White Wool to make Blood-stained Wool, then smelt it into Woven Cruor. Tailor the light set from there: Top Hat or Veil Hat; Dress Coat, Waist Coat, Dress Jacket, or Corset; Trousers, Skirted Trousers, or Skirt; Oxford Boots, Shoes, or Heels.$(br2)Two light pieces now make the current bite draw more blood. Sneak-right-click a villager or player with an empty hand to mesmerise them, spending 50 blood; three light pieces extend that trance. Three light pieces also give a chance to survive otherwise lethal fire damage, and all four pieces make that protection much stronger.
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.medium: The medium set upgrades light clothing with iron: Vampire Helmet from a Top Hat or Veil Hat; Chain Coat from a Dress Coat; Chain Coat (Ladies) from a Dress Jacket; and the exact Resurrected Chestplate from a Waist Coat or Corset. Vampire Leggings and Boots are wearable too, though their old acquisition path still needs a deeper pass.$(br2)Wearing two promoted medium pieces now gives the basic lethal-fire survival chance. Remaining gaps are in-game armor QA, armor model polish, and full old vampire ability timing.
witchery.book.entry.vampirism.stake: A Stake is simple and final. Craft one from a Stick surrounded by Garlic, then use it on a sleeping vampire player to destroy them and consume the Stake.$(br2)The Glass Goblet bridge is also back in first practical form: craft the goblet from glass bottles and glass, then vampires can spend blood to fill it. Drinking a vampire-filled goblet begins vampirism unless the drinker is a werewolf. A Boline-killed Chicken near the old skull rite can fill an empty hotbar goblet with Chicken blood, and using that blood on the skull checks the old night-sky rite without consuming items until Elle exists. Full goblets also validate transfixed, drained villagers near coffins, but the vampire entity handoff is still pending.
witchery.book.entry.lycanthropy.page1: The wolf's curse comes in through a rite, or through the attention of one already afflicted, and it does not announce itself politely. The full moon forces the change. The rest of the time you choose - though choosing becomes harder as the moon waxes.$(br2)In wolf form the body is different in all the ways that matter for fighting: stronger, faster, harder to slow. The mind remains your own, more or less. Find the Wolf Altar and tend it. Mastery matters.
witchery.book.entry.lycanthropy.abilitie: $(li)Strength and speed well beyond a human's in wolf form$(li)Regeneration - the body mends itself$(li)Howling as a weapon, with the right talisman$(li)The Wolf Altar grants mastery from 0 to 3$(li)Mastery 3 is not subtle. Approach with preparation
witchery.book.entry.spirit_world.page1: The world you walk in is not the only world that exists. The Spirit World lies beside it, separated by a boundary that thins around places of power and at the edges of sleep.$(br2)To enter it, drink a Brew of Sleeping near an altar, or eat an Apple of Sleeping. You will leave your body behind. It will wait for you. Try to come back before something finds it.
witchery.book.entry.spirit_world.entry: The Brew of Sleeping carries you across. Your inventory stays behind. Carry only what the spirit world allows - the Icy Needle and a few other items transfer with you.
witchery.book.entry.spirit_world.exit: The Icy Needle brings you back immediately, used up. Dying also returns you, though not comfortably. In absolute emergencies: $(bold)/witchery exit$(/).
witchery.book.entry.dream_weavers.page1: Sleep is not passive, and the spirit world is not a waiting room. A Dream Catcher placed near the sleeping body shapes what happens when consciousness moves through the boundary and returns.$(br2)Different thread weavings produce different effects on waking: Fleet Foot for speed, Iron Arm for strength, Fasting against hunger, Nightmares to shift the dream odds, Intensity to strengthen potions. Only one catcher near you takes effect. Choose deliberately.
witchery.book.entry.dream_weavers.recipe: Fleet Foot follows the old quickness weaving: Item Frame, Fanciful Thread, feathers, Diamond Vapour, Tormented Twine, and long swiftness/slowness splash potions.
Iron Arm uses the same weave frame, but swaps in long strength and weakness splash potions.
Fasting uses a long poison splash potion and Mellifluous Hunger in the opposing potion slot.
Nightmares is the harsher Tormented Twine frame, woven with Diamond Vapour and long poison/night-vision splash potions.
Intensity keeps the old frame but binds Brew of Flowing Spirit against Brew of Sleeping.
witchery.book.entry.crystal_ball.page1: The crystal ball does not tell you what you want to hear. It tells you what it perceives - which is oblique, contextual, and occasionally alarming. Right-click it without an item in hand, with an altar nearby holding at least 500 power, and it will offer a reading.$(br2)There is a cooldown between readings. The ball will not repeat itself. Whether that is a limitation or a mercy is a matter of interpretation.
witchery.book.entry.crystal_ball.recipe: The Crystal Ball is not crafted on a table.
witchery.book.entry.crystal_ball.ritual: Infuse a Quartz Sphere at night on a small ritual circle. Offer a Gold Ingot and Happenstance Oil as support, and keep 2000 altar power ready.
witchery.book.entry.crystal_ball.use: The rite returns a Crystal Ball and attunes it for fortune work. Use it near a powered altar for readings, or focus it with bound waystones and filled taglocks.
witchery.book.entry.brazier.page1: Fire is one of the oldest working tools in the craft, and the brazier is how you direct it. Load up to three ingredients by right-clicking, ignite it with a fire charge or flint and steel, then step back and let it burn.$(br2)Most brazier workings draw power from a nearby altar. The effect releases when the burning is complete. Patience is required - and occasionally a safe distance.
witchery.book.entry.brazier.recipe: Iron ingots and a stick. The brazier does not need to be complicated. What burns inside it, however, often is.
witchery.book.entry.brazier.conjurations: $(li)$(bold)Conjure Spectres$(/) - Wormwood, Bat Wool, Graveyard Dust. Something emerges.$(li)$(bold)Anguish of the Dead$(/) - Tear of Goddess, Blaze Rod, Golden Apple. Strength radiates outward.$(li)$(bold)Deathly Veil$(/) - Fermented Eye, Ender Pearl, Diamond. Light passes through.$(li)$(bold)Fortification of the Corpse$(/) - Tear of Goddess, Diamond, Golden Apple. Resistance, for those nearby.$(li)$(bold)Graveyard Mist$(/) - Nether Wart, Quicklime, Blaze Powder. You will know it by the smoke.
witchery.book.entry.fetishes.page1: A spirit bound to a physical object becomes something useful. The scarecrow that watches with intent, the effigy that senses intrusion, the ladder that extends a boundary - each is a different vessel for the same principle.$(br2)To create a fetish, place the host object in a medium circle with an Attuned Stone, a Necromantic Stone, and a Boline. Sacrifice the required spirits near the circle. The rite binds them to the vessel.
witchery.book.entry.fetishes.effects: $(li)$(bold)Voodoo Protection$(/) - carried protection poppets become more effective nearby$(li)$(bold)Sentinel$(/) - spectres emerge against uninvited guests$(li)$(bold)Shrieking$(/) - emits a redstone pulse and a banshee's cry$(li)$(bold)Disorientation$(/) - armed or armored trespassers find their senses unreliable$(li)$(bold)Ghost Walking$(/) - those walking the spirit world nearby are not hurried back$(br2)Use a Boline to cycle the trigger mode. Use a Taglock Kit to specify who is and is not an intruder.
witchery.book.entry.coffin.page1: A vampire does not sleep in a bed. The sun makes ordinary beds inadvisable, and there is a certain indignity to them regardless. The coffin is better: sealed against daylight, appropriate to the condition, and functional.$(br2)Shift-right-click to open the lid. Right-click to enter and sleep. Any player may use it, but for vampires it resolves the problem of daylight with characteristic directness.
witchery.book.entry.coffin.recipe: Planks, logs, and a bed, in the proportions shown. The result is more durable than it looks.
witchery.book.entry.familiars.page1: A familiar is not merely a tame animal. It is a companion bound to you through ritual, carrying part of your craft onward after the binding is done.$(br2)You may have one familiar at a time. Tame the creature first, then perform the Rite of Familiar Binding. A sitting familiar may be dismissed with a sneaking touch and later recalled through the calling rite when you need it again.$(br2)The binding also leaves the creature strangely resilient: a true familiar now shrugs off fire, long falls, and drowning more like the old craft intended.
witchery.book.entry.familiars.owl: $(bold)The Owl$(/) reads the air around you and warns of what approaches. At full speed on a broomstick, an owl familiar grants a significant additional bonus - they seem to enjoy the height.
witchery.book.entry.familiars.cat: $(bold)The Cat$(/) is indifferent to most things and hostile to supernatural intrusion. Curses directed at you find less purchase when a cat is present, and the same cold attention seems to help your own infernal malice take deeper root when you cast through a proper circle. Whether the cat is aware of this is unclear.
witchery.book.entry.familiars.toad: $(bold)The Toad$(/) is patient, damp, and surprisingly helpful to a brewer. It gathers what falls nearby, gives you the old witch's chance of coaxing an extra bottle from the kettle, and now also strengthens practical brews such as Sprouting, Thorns, Vines, and Erosion when you drink them yourself.
witchery.book.entry.witch_hunter.page1: They exist because we exist. Witch Hunters are organised, motivated, and unpleasant to encounter - they track vampires and werewolves as a profession and take their work seriously.$(br2)They attack at range with a crossbow loaded with silver bolts, and close to melee when necessary. Silver does additional damage to transformed individuals. Silvered armor reduces but does not eliminate this. Plan accordingly.
witchery.book.entry.witch_hunter.desc: Recognisable by the hat, the coat, and the expression of someone who considers their cause righteous. They drop silver bolts and occasionally armour pieces. Their righteousness does not survive them.
witchery.book.entry.creature_traps.page1: Some creatures are better studied after they have stopped moving. The restored traps are low metal plates: place one on the ground, give it a moment to arm, and keep your own feet clear unless you are testing something with unusual confidence.
witchery.book.entry.creature_traps.beart: The Beartrap follows the old iron-and-shears construction. In Rewoven today it catches ordinary living creatures after arming, snaps shut with its old bite, deals four damage, and applies strong slowness. Right-clicking the block opens or closes it again; creative players still spring the jaws but skip the slowing snare.
witchery.book.entry.creature_traps.wolft: The Wolftrap is the silvered variant: upgrade a Beartrap with Silver Deposits or Silver Ingots, Null Catalysts, and Wolfsbane. It remains inert for ordinary beings, but werewolf players can trigger it and suffer the same snap, damage, and slowness, with the same creative snare exception. Like the old silvered trap, it drops nothing when broken.
witchery.book.entry.creature_traps.remai: Old Witchery also used a Wolftrap beside a Wolf Altar, with a sheep as bait under a full moon, to draw a werewolf into a larger curse-spreading setup. That deeper tile-entity path is still future work; the current survival-safe behavior is the craftable trap pair and their direct snap effects.
witchery.book.entry.wicker_man.page1: A Wicker Man is an invitation written in dry bundles and bad judgment. The old world raised straw figures in the wild; the dangerous version is rebuilt from Bloodied Wicker Bundles and burned to call the Horned Huntsman.$(br2)The shape matters. A near miss is only a bonfire.
witchery.book.entry.wicker_man.wicker: Craft Wicker Bundles from nine saplings. Rewoven also treats Witchery saplings as real saplings now, so rowan, alder, and hawthorn can feed the same bundle path once you have grown them.
witchery.book.entry.wicker_man.bloodied: Craft five Bloodied Wicker Bundles from five Wicker Bundles and one Demonic Blood, or use Demonic Blood on placed plain bundles to stain nearby wicker in a small cube. The crafting route is less wasteful when you need all twenty blocks for the figure.
witchery.book.entry.wicker_man.layout: Build one flat, human-shaped wall from exactly twenty Bloodied Wicker Bundles. Bottom to top: $(br)$(bold)XX$()$(br)$(bold)XX$()$(br)$(bold)XXXX$()$(br)$(bold)XXXX$()$(br)$(bold)XXXX$()$(br)$(bold)XX$()$(br)$(bold)XX$()$(br2)Each row is centered above the one below it, so the four-wide body and arms extend one block farther left and right than the two-block legs and head. Leave the neighboring outline cells empty; extra bloodied wicker touching the silhouette spoils the match. Bundle axis affects appearance, but the live matcher checks the bloodied silhouette.
witchery.book.entry.wicker_man.ignition: Use flint and steel on any Bloodied Wicker Bundle in the completed figure. The current port validates the same old seven-layer silhouette, ignites the key bundles, and summons the Horned Huntsman at the base. In-game pose and offset verification is still open, but this is the layout the live matcher checks today.
witchery.book.entry.hobgoblin.page1: Hobgoblins are small, territorial, and largely reasonable as long as you do not disturb their patron. They live in woodland huts, they trade in koboldite - a curious metal found only through their commerce - and they can be led around with appropriate items, which they find irresistible.$(br2)The Statue of Hobgoblin Patron is a fine decoration, but right-clicking it has consequences. You have been told.
witchery.book.entry.hobgoblin.trades: Five trades, each unlocked by completing the previous. Coal into dust. Dust and gold into nuggets. Work upward. The koboldite at the end is genuinely useful.
witchery.blood_crucible.not_ready: You are not powerful enough to commune with this crucible.
witchery.blood_crucible.not_full: The crucible must be full of blood.
witchery.blood_crucible.ultimate.storm: The storm now answers your call.
witchery.blood_crucible.ultimate.farm: Your dominion over mortals is sealed.

witchery.fetish.mode.0: Mode: Trigger if player NOT in list
witchery.fetish.mode.1: Mode: Trigger if player IS in list
witchery.fetish.mode.2: Mode: Trigger if creature not in list
witchery.fetish.mode.3: Mode: Trigger if all not found
witchery.fetish.mode.4: Mode: Trigger if any not found
witchery.ritual.fetish.no_spirits: Not enough spirits nearby to bind.
witchery.ritual.no_circle: No complete ritual circle found here.
witchery.ritual.already_active: That circle is already sustaining an active rite.
witchery.ritual.eclipse.success: The sky darkens... Rite of Total Eclipse complete.
witchery.ritual.eclipse.support: The rite needs quicklime and a stone axe, or quicklime, an iron axe, and a Charged Attuned Stone.
witchery.ritual.eclipse.no_power: A nearby altar lacks the power to darken the sky.
witchery.ritual.beastial_call.success: The creatures answer your call (%s drawn in).
witchery.ritual.beastial_call.started: The creatures hear your distant call.
witchery.ritual.beastial_call.no_power: A nearby altar lacks the power to call the beasts.
witchery.ritual.transpose_ores.success: The circle begins drawing hidden ore to the surface.
witchery.ritual.transpose_ores.support: The rite needs an ender pearl, iron ingot, blaze powder, and a Charged Attuned Stone.
witchery.ritual.natures_power.success: Wild growth answers the circle's call.

item.witchery.immortals_observations_boo: A doomed scholar's account of discourse with the undead
The first pages warn that the author studied an immortal predator and wrote for those who would survive the lesson.
A chicken, a skull, a boline, and a glass goblet begin the old blood rite.
A night rite calls string, red dust, torches, and a skull beneath open stars.
Blood poured over the skull draws Lilith's attention and sends the seeker toward the Nether.
Strength is proven to her in battle; the filled goblet begins the curse.
The first hunger fades only after feeding, and the body starts to change.
Mesmerised victims can be held still, but draining too deeply has consequences.
After mastery, the vampire begins to sense time, hunger, and sunlight differently.
Sunlight can be collected and turned back on the curse until the burning dulls.
Blazes and fortress fire mark the next trial of endurance.
Greater strength brings stone-breaking power and a second appeal to Lilith.
A red flower and another filled goblet open the path to higher mastery.
Flight follows; distance and village walls matter less than before.
Transfixed victims can be guided into cages for careful feeding.
Power over blood becomes power over making new vampires.
The final note describes a coffin, a goblet, and an unwilling rebirth.
